name: review-recency
question: Did I already run a heavy periodic review/refactor skill (e.g. /0-uldf-scrutinize, /0-uldf-uladp-compliance) on THIS project recently — such that re-running it now would be redundant?
cost_provenance: estimated 2026-07-03 -- one review-recency.sh reader pass (jq over command-usage/*.jsonl, project-scoped) on the ULDF framework repo under Git Bash (win32; slowest supported environment); pessimistic-honest per ORACLE-COST-01

schema.recent: boolean (true when >=1 covered skill ran on this project within recentDays)

details.recentSkills: array of {skill, lastUsed, lastArg1} — covered skills whose most-recent run on this project is within recentDays

schema.briefing: string (empty when recent=false; one-liner suitable for ORACLE BRIEFING when recent=true)

fallback: Run scripts/review-recency.sh --project "$(basename "$PWD")" --json and read .projects[0].skills; a covered skill with status=="recent" means it ran on this project within recentDays. The same reader powers /0-uldf-portfolio recency (cross-project) and the in-skill guard in /0-uldf-scrutinize + /0-uldf-uladp-compliance.

provenance.note: Per-project briefing consumer of the review-recency reader (RECENCY-01). Emits nothing on the common path (no covered skill run within recentDays); gracefully absent on NO-DATA (no usage registry). The direct 'don't re-run' defense is the in-skill guard (RECENCY-05); this briefing is the passive heads-up. DEC-139.
